notes_for_editor: Thin record: the NHLR detail page is the only substantive source. Its build, cab, transfer, administration, staffing and registration facts all come from that one page. The Forest Lookouts Butte County listing has only a February 23, 1929 quote about a planned 60-foot steel tower on Baldy Peak, east of Stirling City; it does not name Bald Mountain. The tower record data/towers/ca/us-ca-bald-mountain-cal-fire-butte-county.json has height_m 18.3, which equals 60 feet and so may have come from the Baldy Peak quote. No source read gives this lookout's height, so height_m is left out of facts and story. Please confirm or remove height_m in that tower record. Checked 2026-10-08: the register footer (raw crawl cache) reads "Last updated on July 31, 2020", which dates the page, not the staffing note. Not in facts or story: a search snippet for the Butte County Battalion 1 page (buttecounty.ca.gov/553/Battalion-1) says the lookout is no longer staffed by lookout personnel and has two ALERTCalifornia cameras. That page returns HTTP 403 to both fetch_text and WebFetch, so it is not footnoted, and the snippet is not quoted. A human should check it, because it would change the staffing and today sections. The transfer to CDF is dated only to the late 1950s, so no event year is given. Staffing has no as_of date: the register footer says the page was last updated July 31, 2020, but our reader drops that footer, so it is not cited. Access, climbability and current condition are unknown and left out. No fire history was found in the sources read. Searches returned other Bald Mountains (Maine, Idaho, Inyo, Mono, Sierra, Sequoia and El Dorado National Forests), which were excluded. No photos added; the record's three NHLR photos are all-rights-reserved.
